cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll manage this tap repair properly. The drip gives us a reason to replace the sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs a washer. I've bought one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, we'll use yours. While the sink's out, I'll replace the swollen worktop. You choose the finish; I want you happy with it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That worktop runs under every cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we can finally fix the layout. You sketch where you'd like the cupboards; I'll arrange to empty the whole kitchen. We won't waste the chance your washer has opened up.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 manages confidently; A3 adopts B washer and grants finish choice, while A5 offers layout control to keep cooperation with ever larger disruption.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 washer causes A3 incorporation in sink/worktop project; B4 all cupboards causes A5 whole-kitchen emptying and layout revision.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies a purchased small solution and B4 a real physical complication; A welcomes both as input instead of dismissing the partner.

heightening.evidence: A5 promotes the dependency warning into permission for the largest project yet.

specificity.evidence: A1 tap, A3 swollen worktop and B4 cupboard relationship keep the scope progression concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 washer opening a chance is an exaggerated credit claim, grounded in the actual purchased object.
